title: Golden-path Terraform module for Private EKS control plane bootstrap and post-upgrade healthkit
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a single, well-documented Terraform module that creates a production-ready Redwood Private EKS control plane (VPC, control plane configuration, IAM roles, KMS integration) using an operatorless, idempotent ‘golden-path’ flow, and adds lightweight post-upgrade health verification hooks and telemetry.

Scope: The module must: provision EKS control plane resources in a customer VPC, create least-privileged IAM roles for control plane and bootstrap agents, wire customer KMS keys for secrets and cluster encryption, emit telemetry-friendly tags and resource names, and expose modular inputs for canary bootstrap vs full fleet. It will also install a thin, optional validation job (Kubernetes Job + ClusterRole binding) that runs after Terraform apply or during controlled upgrade windows to perform smoke checks: API server sanity, node bootstrap success, API responsiveness (simple echo), and sample workload lifecycle.

Non-goals: This module will not: manage application-level manifests beyond the validation job, run long-running operators, or replace customer-specific network provisioning. Deep chaos or expensive e2e tests are out of scope; those live in CI.

Design constraints and decisions: idempotency is the highest priority. Every resource must be re-apply-safe and include stable tags/labels. For upgrades we will implement a two-phase hook: preflight validators (Terraform null_resource provisioner using local-exec with awscli/kubectl where possible) and a post-upgrade validation job that the CI or runbook can poll. Avoid irreversible actions by preferring CRD-less checks and ClusterRole minimization. KMS integration will support both customer-managed keys (CMK) and customer-provided alias; we will surface a boolean toggle and validate key policy with a static analyzer step in CI.

Observability and telemetry: the module will emit CloudWatch and Prometheus-friendly resource tags, and create a lightweight S3 bucket for healthkit logs (optional, encrypted). Terraform outputs will include URLs to health snapshot, the validation job run ID, and a short diagnostic payload.

Rollback/upgrade safety: The module will include an optional staged rollout flag: when enabled, the module creates a canary control plane (isolated subnet) and runs validation before switching the production route. This is intended for customers on Dedicated fleets; flag default is false.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module with documented inputs/outputs and examples (canary/full).
- CI validation pipeline (terrafmt/terraform validate/tflint/checkov + post-apply smoke test).
- Runbook for manual upgrades and tips for trimming IAM permissions.
- Acceptance tests (lightweight) and sample GH PR ready to review.

Risks & mitigations:
- KMS policy misconfiguration: add static policy linter and an opt-in dry-run validate step.
- Long-running validation jobs blocking apply: keep validation job TTL short and make it optional.
- Drift from cluster changes: emit drift telemetry and integrate with existing drift detector job.
acceptance_criteria: Module provisions EKS control plane (managed) in a provided VPC with idempotent terraform apply loops
IAM roles created follow least-privilege patterns and pass static linter rules in CI
KMS key wiring supports CMK alias and fails fast with clear error messages if policy is incompatible
Optional post-apply health validation job runs, reports results to an S3 log object and Terraform outputs validation URL
Module supports canary flag that provisions isolated control plane resources and exposes documented rollback steps
Comprehensive examples in README: minimal bootstrap, canary rollout, and upgrade path
Automated CI pipeline runs terraform validate/tflint/checkov and a post-apply smoke test against a short-lived test account
